title: Deal with safety, health and environmental emergencies in the workplace

lessons.title: Types of emergencies and raising the alarm
lessons.html:
Types of emergencies

An emergency is a sudden event that puts people, property or the environment in danger and needs action at once. At a grain silo or farm, emergencies include:

  • Fire: in a dryer, a bin, a store, a vehicle or the veld.
  • Dust explosion: grain dust in the air can explode when it meets a spark or flame.
  • Engulfment: a person trapped or buried in flowing grain inside a bin or truck.
  • Injuries: falls from heights, caught in conveyors or augers, crush injuries from vehicles.
  • Chemical incidents: fumigant gas leaks, fuel or chemical spills.
  • Medical emergencies: heart attack, heat stroke, severe allergy.
  • Environmental incidents: oil or chemical running into a drain, river or dam.
  • Severe weather: lightning, hail, floods.

Raising the alarm

  1. Shout a warning to people nearby.
  2. Use the alarm system at your site: siren, bell, horn or radio call.
  3. Phone the emergency numbers on the notice board. Know them before an emergency happens.
  4. Give clear information: what happened, where, how many people are hurt, and any danger such as gas or fire.

Know your site emergency plan

Every workplace must have an emergency plan. Make sure you know:

  • The alarm sound and what it means.
  • The escape routes and emergency exits from your work area.
  • The assembly point.
  • Where the fire extinguishers, fire hoses, first aid box and spill kit are.
  • Who the first aiders and fire wardens are.

Take part in emergency drills seriously. Practice makes the right actions automatic when you are frightened.

lessons.title: Responding safely to an emergency
lessons.html:
Responding safely

The first rule: do not become a second victim. Check for danger before you go to help.

Fire

  • Raise the alarm first.
  • Fight a small fire only if you are trained, it is safe, and you have an escape route behind you.
  • Use the right extinguisher. Never use water on electrical or fuel fires.
  • If the fire grows, leave, close doors behind you and go to the assembly point.
  • Never go back in to fetch belongings.

Person trapped in grain

  • Shout for help and call the emergency team.
  • Stop all grain flow: switch off and lock out unloading equipment.
  • Never go into the bin to rescue unless you are a trained rescuer with a harness and lifeline. Untrained rescuers often get trapped too.

Injury

  • Switch off machinery and make the area safe.
  • Call a first aider. Give first aid only if you are trained.
  • Do not move a person with a possible back or neck injury unless they are in more danger where they are.
  • If the person is not breathing normally, call for an ambulance and start CPR if trained: hard, fast chest compressions in the centre of the chest.

First aid and CPR must be learnt through hands-on training with an accredited provider.

Spills and gas

  • Keep away from fumigant gas. Leave the area, move upwind, and stop others from entering.
  • For a fuel or oil spill: stop the source if safe, use the spill kit to contain it, and keep it out of drains and water.

After the emergency

  • Go to the assembly point and be counted.
  • Report what you saw to your supervisor.
  • Every incident must be reported and investigated so it does not happen again. The OHS Act 85 of 1993 requires certain incidents to be reported.
  • Ask for support if you feel shocked or upset. That is normal.

Key points

  • Know the alarm, escape routes, assembly point and emergency numbers.
  • Raise the alarm first and give clear information.
  • Do not become a second victim.
  • Never enter a grain bin to rescue unless trained and equipped.
  • Report every incident.

options.text: Run in as fast as you can
Do not become a second victim
Wait for the manager before doing anything

quiz.question: What can cause a dust explosion?

options.text: Grain dust in the air meeting a spark or flame

quiz.question: A worker is trapped in grain in a bin. What must you do?

options.text: Climb in and pull them out
Keep the auger running to drain the grain
Call for help, stop grain flow, and only trained rescuers with lifelines enter
